subagent_reports.topic: Validate PokeEdge store-consolidation recovery design before design gate

sources.label: resolveConsolidationTargetIds
sources.summary: Target defaults to resolveProjectIdentity(directory) structural git-root identity; 'unstable' resolution refuses with guidance; SHA40-validated; source==target rejected. Confirms claim (1): true-root bdf259aa resolves as default target; stale 4d6b5898 only used if explicitly passed.

sources.label: executeConsolidation guards
sources.summary: Hard-fails with typed ConsolidationError before any mutation: approval_required (approvedByUser!==true or blank evidence), worker_lock_live (plan.safety.source_worker_lock_live), collisions_present (>0). Confirms claims (2)+(3).

sources.label: Terminal-first phased execution + abort
sources.summary: Phase 1 imports ALL terminal items before ANY live recreation; terminal import failure returns finishExecuteReport immediately (aborts before live phase) so history stays correct with only live work to retry. Confirms partial-failure safety (3).

sources.label: Ledger-aware collision + idempotence planning
sources.summary: Ledger read BEFORE collision detection; ledgered items present in both stores treated as expected post-consolidation state (skip_ledgered), not collisions. Keyed on (source,target,item_id). Confirms claim (4).

sources.label: Worker-lock probe (read-only, liveness-checked)
sources.summary: probeWorkerLock parses worker.lock pid and checks isProcessAlive; source_worker_lock_live = present && live===true. Only LIVE lock blocks; stale locks do not. Never reclaims/kills (honors C3).

sources.label: Guard + idempotence tests
sources.summary: Tests assert approval_required, worker_lock_live, collisions_present typed refusals; 'second run after success is a reported no-op via ledger' (no_op:true, all skipped, no new rows, no collisions); 'interrupted run resumes' (crash after arch-a ledgered before term-a -> re-run skips arch-a, applies term-a). Proves guards + crash-safe idempotence enforced, not just coded.

sources.label: Approved strict ChangeContract (12 items)
sources.summary: Design AC/constraints (dry_run zero mutations, approval-gated execute, halt on collision/lock/validation, preserve sources, post-execute idempotence evidence) map 1:1 to the tool's coded guards and tests.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is a thin correct orchestration of an already-implemented well-guarded tool (adv_store_consolidate, parent fixShallowRepoIdentity). All four validation targets backed by source + tests: (1) target resolution defaults to structural true-root identity bdf259aa, stale 4d6b5898 superseded in agreement/design and never passed; (2) dry_run read-only, execute approval-gated with typed approval_required refusal; (3) collision per-ID halt, live worker-lock liveness-checked and never reclaimed, partial-failure terminal-first abort-before-live all coded and tested; (4) append-only ledger keyed on (source,target,item_id) yields no-op re-runs and crash-resume, ledgered-in-both exempt from collision. Design treats tool implementation as out-of-scope (OOS1) and sequences one source at a time. No architectural deviation from by-the-book recovery pattern.

validation.notes: All four targets confirmed against store-consolidate.ts and store-consolidate.test.ts. Design is a safe procedural application of a tested tool. Minor non-blocking advisories only.

tradeoffs: Ledger idempotence is content-hash + (source,target,item_id) keyed rather than transactional; crash between projection copy and ledger append could re-copy a bundle on resume, but cp is overwrite-safe and re-appending is deduped by the ledger read: no corruption, only benign redundant copy.

Live-phase failures (change/Epic recreation) record per-item 'failed' outcomes and do NOT abort the run (unlike terminal-phase), so a live recreation failure yields a partial-success report the operator must inspect; design step 5 post-execute dry-run and partial-response handling cover this.

alternatives_considered.option: Pass target_project_id=bdf259aa explicitly instead of relying on default resolution
alternatives_considered.rationale: Low-cost hardening: removes dependency on run-location identity resolution and makes AC5 evidence self-documenting. Not required for PASS since resolution is deterministic from git root and the tool rejects 'unstable'.
Not the current true-root identity; agreement explicitly supersedes it with bdf259aa. Using it would consolidate into a wrong store.

alternatives_considered.option: Batch both sources in one execute or auto-approve
alternatives_considered.rationale: One-source-at-a-time + explicit per-run approval preserves auditable per-item outcomes and halt-before-partial-overwrite semantics (AC2, AC3, C4).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to design gate completion; design PASSES. Non-blocking hardening: (a) pass target_project_id=bdf259aa162ae192af5b18899ccdc653b085528d explicitly on every dry_run/execute; (b) re-run dry_run immediately before the execute approval so plan-presented equals plan-executed; (c) treat any live-phase 'failed' outcome as a hard stop for operator inspection before the next source.

subagent_reports.recommendation: PASS. All four targets verified against source + tests. Complete design gate. Optional hardening: explicit target_project_id on all invocations; re-run dry_run at approval checkpoint; treat live-phase failed outcomes as inspect-before-continue.

subagent_reports.topic: Bounded source-Epic state query timeout in adv_store_consolidate

sources.label: Local impl: store-consolidate.ts queryLiveEpicState + live-Epic recreation
sources.summary: handle.query(getEpicStateQuery) at line 1368 has no client-side deadline/abort. Per-item try/catch (1493-1501) already normalizes any throw into a per-item 'failed' outcome preserving item_id+action+error. writeLedger (1479) runs only AFTER successful recreate, so a thrown timeout writes no ledger row. Connection.close() is in a finally (1503-1508) closing once after the live phase.

sources.label: Local impl: ConsolidationExecuteDeps seam
sources.summary: queryLiveEpicState is an injectable dep (projectId, epicId) => Promise<EpicWorkflowState | null>. This is the exact, minimal seam to wrap with a bounded timeout without touching terminal-first/collision/lock/idempotence logic.

sources.label: Local tests: existing unavailable-state precedent
sources.summary: 'missing source epic workflow state fails that item without crashing the run' asserts report.success=false, epic outcome status 'failed', error /state/i, and terminal items still applied. A timeout test is a direct structural sibling of this case.

sources.label: Temporal TS SDK — CallContext deadline/abortSignal
sources.summary: CallContext exposes deadline?: number|Date (gRPC per-request deadline) and abortSignal?: AbortSignal. These are the SDK-native client-side request-bounding primitives; deadline applies to individual requests, distinct from connectTimeout.

sources.label: Temporal TS SDK — _queryWorkflowHandler retry path
sources.summary: queryWorkflow RPC flows through the retry interceptor (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED/UNAVAILABLE retried). WorkflowHandle.query(queryDef) takes no per-call CallContext, so an unanswered query can retry/block up to the tool budget — confirming the unbounded-hang root cause. Deadline/abort must be applied at connection/interceptor level or via a host-side Promise.race timeout wrapper around the query seam.

sources.label: Temporal TS SDK — Connection.connect default connectTimeout
sources.summary: Default connectTimeoutMs is 10_000ms. connectTimeout bounds only initial connection establishment, NOT the query RPC — so it does not by itself bound queryLiveEpicState.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The design correctly targets the unbounded handle.query() at store-consolidate.ts:1368 as the sole hang source, verified against the observed 10s ToolExecutionTimeout on the 67fe3e95 execute. Three of the four required invariants are ALREADY structurally guaranteed by existing code and need only preservation, not new mechanism: (1) typed per-item 'failed' normalization exists in the live-Epic catch (1493-1501) and is proven by test 1282-1310; (2) no-ledger-write-on-failure is guaranteed because writeLedger is sequenced after recreate inside the try, so any throw skips it; (3) terminal-first/collision/lock/idempotence live in separate phases (approval check 1209-1218, lock refusal 1223, terminal Phase 1 1268-1335, ledger idempotence via skip_ledgered) untouched by wrapping the query seam. The one genuinely new element is the bounded timeout itself. SDK evidence shows WorkflowHandle.query() has no per-call deadline argument, so the correct placement is a host-side timeout wrapper (Promise.race with a timer, or AbortController) around the injectable queryLiveEpicState dep — below the ~10s tool ceiling (design says strictly below; a 6-8s bound leaves margin for the surrounding terminal phase and report assembly). This is the boring, proven approach and it composes with the existing dep seam and existing error normalization with near-zero blast radius. CAUTION (non-blocking) items: (a) client resource cleanup on timeout — current finally closes the connection once after the live phase, which is correct for a per-item timeout that does NOT abort the shared connection; but if the timeout wrapper leaves the underlying gRPC query promise pending (Promise.race does not cancel the loser), the SDK retry loop may keep the connection busy until connection.close() in finally forcibly tears it down. Design item 3 ('client resources close on timeout/failure') should be interpreted as: the existing finally close is sufficient IF the wrapper does not open a new client per item; do not add a per-item connection.close inside the loop or it will break subsequent items sharing the memoized bundle (getClient at 1340-1343 memoizes one bundle). (b) The 'not found' -> null branch (1370) must remain distinct from timeout: a timeout must throw (become 'failed'), not be coerced to null (which would be treated as unavailable-state — same outcome class, but the error text should say timeout for AC6 failure-class evidence). (c) A leaked pending query promise after Promise.race should be swallowed (attach a .catch(()=>{}) ) to avoid an unhandledRejection when the retry eventually errors post-timeout.

validation.notes: Design is sound and low-risk. It correctly localizes the fix to the unbounded query, preserves all four required invariants (three already structural), and matches SDK-native bounding semantics. PASS with three non-blocking CAUTION refinements to encode in tests/impl: (1) do not add per-item connection.close inside the shared-bundle loop; rely on the existing finally; (2) timeout must throw a distinct typed error (surface 'timeout'/failure-class text for AC6), never coerce to the not-found null path; (3) swallow the post-race leaked query rejection to avoid unhandledRejection.

tradeoffs: Host-side Promise.race/AbortController timeout wrapper is needed because WorkflowHandle.query() exposes no per-call gRPC deadline; the SDK-native CallContext.deadline is only reachable at connection/interceptor scope, which would bound ALL calls rather than just the source-Epic query.

Promise.race does not cancel the losing query promise, so the underlying gRPC retry loop keeps running until the shared connection is closed in the existing finally; acceptable for a single-shot per-item bound but requires swallowing the leaked rejection.

Choosing a timeout strictly below the 10s tool ceiling trades a small risk of aborting a slow-but-healthy query for a hard guarantee that execute never hangs the tool boundary; a 6-8s bound is the reasonable middle.

alternatives_considered.option: Set CallContext.deadline via a client interceptor at bundle creation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Applies to every RPC on the shared client (recreate signals, change starts), not just the source-Epic query; over-broad and could destabilize the healthy recreate path. The seam-scoped wrapper is more precise.

alternatives_considered.option: AbortController + abortSignal on a per-item CallContext
alternatives_considered.rationale: WorkflowHandle.query(queryDef) has no CallContext parameter, so abortSignal cannot be attached per-.query() call without dropping to workflowService.queryWorkflow directly. A Promise.race timeout around the dep is simpler and equally deterministic; AbortController is a valid future refinement if the SDK exposes per-call context.

alternatives_considered.option: Retry loop inside the tool after timeout
alternatives_considered.rationale: Design boundary and agreement C4 mandate deterministic single-shot failure for operator-controlled retry; an internal retry loop would violate no-polling and the stop-and-surface contract.

alternatives_considered.option: Coerce timeout to the existing not-found null path
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would lose the timeout/failure-class distinction required by AC6 evidence. Timeout must throw distinct typed text; null is reserved for genuine not-found.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed. Implement a host-side bounded timeout (Promise.race with a timer set strictly below the 10s tool budget, ~6-8s) wrapping the injectable queryLiveEpicState dep; on timeout throw a distinct typed error whose message names the timeout and source epic id so it lands in the existing per-item 'failed' outcome and AC6 failure-class evidence. Do NOT add a per-item connection.close inside the shared-bundle loop — keep relying on the existing finally connection.close (1503-1508). Swallow the leaked post-race query rejection. Keep terminal-first, lock/collision refusal, approval gate, and ledger idempotence untouched.

subagent_reports.recommendation: PASS. The bounded-source-Epic-timeout design is architecturally correct and low-risk. Encode three test-backed refinements: (1) a fake queryLiveEpicState that never resolves must produce a per-item 'failed' outcome within the bound while terminal items stay applied and NO ledger row is written for the epic (mirrors existing test 1282-1310); (2) assert the shared Temporal bundle is closed exactly once via the existing finally and that a per-item timeout does not close/reopen the connection mid-loop; (3) assert timeout error text is distinct from the not-found path and carries failure-class info for AC6. All existing consolidation tests (idempotence 1134-1184, resume 1186+, no-delete 1312-1329, collision, lock) must remain green to prove preserved safety (C5).
follow_ups: Impl/test: verify getClient bundle memoization (lines 1340-1343) is not broken by the timeout wrapper — one bundle, one finally close.

# Agreement: Bound source-Epic recovery

## Objective
Deliver a tested bounded source-Epic state-query recovery path in `adv_store_consolidate`, then release it from `trunk`. The linked child `runPokeedgeRecovery` owns all live PokeEdge consolidation after this release.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Source Epic state retrieval returns within the 10s ADV tool boundary: success returns state; timeout returns a typed, actionable per-item failure naming the Epic; it never hangs execute.
2. A timeout writes no Epic ledger row, attempts no Epic recreation, and preserves terminal-first processing, explicit execute approval, lock/collision refusal, source preservation, and idempotence.
3. Tests prove a 6–8s default bound, late rejection observation, no false timeout, one shared Temporal bundle, and one awaited connection close before execution resolves.
4. Focused consolidation tests pass and repository validation is clean.
5. Parent release occurs from the approved change branch to `trunk`; no live PokeEdge store is consolidated by this parent.

## Constraints
- No manual Epic reconstruction or source deletion.
- No live consolidation against a branch-built tool.
- Tool changes remain focused on timeout and cleanup behavior.
- Parent live-operation tasks remain cancelled; only linked child `runPokeedgeRecovery` may perform live recovery after parent release.

## Out of scope
- Live PokeEdge store consolidation, deferred to linked child `runPokeedgeRecovery`.
- Further consolidation-tool features.
- Source-store deletion.

# Design: Release bounded query recovery

## Delivered implementation
- A 7s host-side `Promise.race` bound wraps every source live-Epic query at the injectable seam.
- `EpicQueryTimeoutError` carries Epic ID, timeout, and remediation; timeout lands in existing per-item failed outcome rather than the `null`/not-found path.
- Losing query rejection is observed; shared Temporal client connection closes once in existing `finally`, now awaited.
- Focused direct and default-path lifecycle tests prove timeout non-mutation, one shared bundle, and close completion before operation result.

## Release sequencing
1. Parent releases only this implementation and tests from its isolated branch.
2. Archive preflight verifies test/review/contract evidence and trunk release proof.
3. Linked child `runPokeedgeRecovery` begins only after parent is released and deployed from trunk; it refreshes dry-runs and obtains its own execute approval.

## Boundaries
No live store operation, source deletion, manual reconstruction, or new consolidation feature belongs to this parent.

## Outcome
The consolidation tool now fails a stalled source-Epic state query within 7 seconds instead of consuming the 10-second ADV tool budget. The failure identifies the Epic and directs operators to restore the source workflow and rerun safely.

## Value
PokeEdge recovery can proceed from deployed trunk without a hanging execute call or manual Epic reconstruction. Live recovery is intentionally deferred to linked child `runPokeedgeRecovery` after this fix is released.

## Verification
- Timeout, late-rejection, no-false-timeout, no-ledger-write, one-bundle, and awaited-close behavior: 44 focused tests passed.
- Repository validation: `pnpm run check` passed.
- Acceptance review: READY after removing manual-reconstruction guidance from failure messages.

## Risks and follow-up
- No live store was changed by this parent.
- Child `runPokeedgeRecovery` must refresh dry-runs and obtain execute approval from deployed trunk before operating on either source store.

## Release Readiness Summary
Release-ready code and tests. Parent contains only bounded-query recovery; its four former live-operation tasks are cancelled and explicitly owned by the linked child. No migration, data, or frontend impact.
